description:
Goal: a binary is ONE concept in fz, bytes plus a bit length, with one home in the runtime and one in the compiler. Every binary operation compiles to the optimal machine sequence for it. Priorities, in order: consistency, consolidation, conceptual folding, elegance, speed.

METHOD (user, 2026-11-18): optimal assembly FIRST, then the compiler. For each operation:
1. Hand-write the optimal arm64 sequence: the target listing. Make it a sequence the compiler could emit given facts it has or should have, and annotate each instruction with the fact that licenses it, e.g. "lane proven binary", "position is the constant 0", "cursor is byte-aligned".
2. Count it, and check it against the probe's slope where it can be run.
3. Then change the compiler and runtime until the emitted listing IS the target, or differs only in ways the ticket records and explains.

A target listing that needs a fact the compiler lacks names that fact. Missing facts are the conceptual work: data model up, correct by construction.

Diagnosis (audit on develop 37c5473cd):
- A binary is stored three ways (inline <=64 B, view onto a SharedBin, read-only literal object). The compiler adds a fourth, the cursor (source, bit position).
- About 24 runtime functions decode (ptr, len), 13 of them by hand, with three failure styles: panic, sentinel, abort.
- 6 byte-equality implementations. 5 match-region walkers. 2 construction paths (<> and the constructor) that share nothing.
- Each extern re-checks a tag the compiler proved 3-9 times. A share call that is a no-op for binaries costs 42 instructions, 1-4 times per operation.
- Matching is the model to copy: 29 instructions per byte, against the BEAM's 284.

Cost on develop (instructions per op, local slope 100k/300k, includes a 22-instruction loop; BEAM JIT in parentheses):

| Operation | fz | BEAM |
|---|---|---|
| byte_size | 95 | 42 |
| byte_size(literal) | 49 | folded |
| a == b | 500 | 239 |
| a == "true" | 385 | — |
| case a do "true" | ~34 | — |
| acc <> "ab" | 376 | 1213 |
| growing <> plus later byte_size | 448 | 89 |
| <<acc::binary, x::binary>> | 1667 | — |
| same, growing | 173,841, quadratic | 162 |
| <<a::8, b::16, c::binary>> | 1759 | 231 |
| 4 B slice | 653 | 156 |
| binary through a non-inlined call | +183 | — |

Judging: A/B guards are judged on bench (ssh bench, BENCH_BUSY lock). Local slopes are iteration aids.

Durable materials: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-binaries/
- runtime.md (R1-R25)
- compiler.md (C1-C17)
- machine.md (M1-M14)
- tickets.md (board map: overlaps, stale tickets, gaps)
- listings/: fz traces and static listings per probe, beam/ reference
- probes/ and listings/probes/: the probe templates and slope harness (m.sh, tr.sh, trace.py)
- verify/
- proposal.html

Proposal page: https://claude.ai/artifact/Wb77AvyLphyW8L6XmsMLL7

Related, owned elsewhere (coordinate directly with the owner; do not duplicate):
- fz-nml.29, private append, is owned by Optimize. Its ticket 2b ("a share is one store") is the same seam as this epic's share child.
- Invalid UTF-8 semantics belong to Elixir Parity: fz-sc8.107 + fz-rua fold into fz-mue.4.
- fz-mue.5 and fz-mue.6 (:erlang/:binary exports) belong to Elixir Parity.
- Off-heap binary bytes driving collection (R19) plus fz-9x7.40 and fz-9x7.8 belong to GC.

Proposed board hygiene, NOT applied; it needs user approval through Coordinator:
- Close fz-sc8.112, fz-sc8.89 and fz-sc8.195.
- Re-describe fz-sc8.183.10 and fz-sc8.231.
- Fold fz-sc8.183.4 into .9.
- Fix the ProcBin/stub wording in nml.1, sc8.208, 9x7.8 and sc8.111.
fz-sc8.111 and the remaining open fz-sc8.183 work are superseded by children here once those land.

Not in scope: the general codegen items found in the listings. These are checked arithmetic at 5 instructions where 2 would do, adrp/blr extern calls, frame-lane kind dispatch, the forwarder after a call return, a continuation for a callee that cannot suspend, and send's SipHash. They are listed in machine.md M9/M12-M14 and will be proposed separately.

Acceptance:
- Every child is closed.
- Each operation's emitted listing matches its target listing, recorded in the repo.
- The decode, equality, walker and construction counts have fallen to one each.
- All three paths raise ArgumentError for bad binary input where Elixir does.
title: A binary is bytes and a length: one concept, optimal machine code
